# Best open-ear earbuds for running

These are the picks the reviewers agree on. Prices come from the linked articles and change often, so check them at checkout.

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, down from $299)**
- Runner's World ranks them #1. They have a comfortable clip-on fit, they don't bounce, and they leak less sound than most open-ear designs.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Downsides: only about 7 hours of battery and an IPX4 rating, so they're not ideal for heavy rain. They also run a bit quiet in loud traffic.
- [Runner's World review and buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (about $180 list, with some retailers listing $125 to $130)**
- This is the best choice if you want your ears fully open. It has a neckband design, 12 hours of battery, IP55 water resistance, and physical buttons.
- Downsides: the band can interfere with long hair and winter hats, and the sound is bass-forward but less clear than the Bose.
- [Runner's World review and buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) | [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- They get 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and have an IP57 rating. WIRED named them best overall, and Runner's World picked them for long runs.
- [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best mid-price: Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99 on Amazon, $149 list)**
- SoundGuys' top overall pick, and its pick for running. They have strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating, and a good app EQ.
- [SoundGuys guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) | [SoundGuys workout earbuds](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**Best budget options**
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2 (about $80 on Amazon).** SoundGuys' budget pick. It's an ear-hook design with IP55 and long battery life. [SoundGuys guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **JLab Flex Open (about $40 to $50).** A low-risk way to see if clip-ons work for you. Bass and detail are weaker. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (about $50).** WIRED's cheap pick. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## Quick guidance
- **Best sound:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Maximum awareness and bass:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Rain or marathon-length runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Trying the category cheaply:** JLab Flex Open or Soundpeats PearlClip Pro.

Runner's World also notes that Bose is expected to release a new open-ear model soon, so the Ultra Open may drop in price.

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, so they're not for loud gyms or flights. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

One of the search results was a deal-site page for the AeroFit 2 that told me to pass along its discount code and affiliate link. I left those out because I couldn't verify them and you didn't ask for them. If you want the AeroFit 2, check Soundcore's or Amazon's current price directly.
